region: Burdett · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Atwater Estate Vineyards lies on the southern end of Seneca Lake’s east side, near the village of Hector. The site was once Rolling Vineyards, whose owners won the first New York Governor’s Cup. After that winery closed in 1989, the vines were kept up, and in 1999 Ted Marks and Phil Hazlitt bought the 84-acre property. Vinny Aliperti, who trained at Wölffer Estate and Hermann J. Wiemer, has led the winemaking since the early 2000s. About 60 acres are planted to some fifteen grapes: native, hybrid and European vinifera.

This is one of Atwater’s skin-fermented, or “orange,” wines. White grapes are fermented on their skins, as red wines are, an ancient technique that gives an amber colour, gentle tannin and savoury depth. Here two aromatic grapes are blended: Gewürztraminer, the spicy, rose-scented vinifera of Alsace, and Vignoles, a French-American hybrid prized in the Finger Lakes for its bright acidity and stone-fruit character. Expect a richly textured, savoury and earthy wine with orange marmalade, grapefruit rind and dried flowers on the finish.
facts: About 60 planted acres on Seneca Lake’s east shore
